While correlations had been increasing during the selloff, Xu says that changed Friday:

Friday’s move was about idiosyncratic risk, not macro: Single stock vol outpaced the increase in index vol on Friday, with the VIXEQSM Index jumping over 11 pts to a 1-year high of 58% (vs. VIX Index up 7pts). 

In other words, expected dispersion increased even as the market sold off almost 4%, as can be seen in the DSPXSM Index rising 5 pts on Friday (see Exhibit 3). 

This comes as investors rotate out of the AI theme into other sectors, rather than selling everything indiscriminately. As tech stocks fall out of favor, Tech vols have risen the most, with QQQ 1M implied vol jumping over 20 pts last week, the most of any global index. In contrast, US small cap volatility, which has very little exposure to the AI theme, saw its volatility trail that of its large-cap counterparts. The RTY-SPX 1M implied vol spread narrowed to a 6-year low of 1.4% as a result.
tweets.quoted_tweet_text:
CBOE's Mandy Xu: Friday’s VIX move, while large, was  surprisingly orderly. The sell-off in SPX® spot (-3.7%) and the  increase in fixed-strike vols (+3.2 pts) accounted for almost  90% of the 7.4pt VIX increase. 

Very little came from demand for downside puts. In fact, changes in skew and convexity contributed just 0.9pt to the VIX move (see Exhibit 2). In contrast, demand for downside protection made up almost half of the Nov 5th VIX spike. This can also be seen in  measures of SPX 1M skew (25-delta ratio), which spiked to  the 95th percentile high after the Nov 5th sell-off but only  steepened modestly to the 80th percentile last Friday. 

Also  notable was the lack of demand for upside calls on Friday, with call skew falling and call convexity unchanged. It seems that while there was little panic on Friday, investors were also not positioning for a quick rebound.

We're thrilled to invest in Embo.

Robots can already do remarkable things in demos, but those skills are fragile. Move an object, change the lighting, or introduce something unfamiliar, and the robot can struggle.

@EmboAI is building the brain for the humanoid workforce. They start by training a world model on massive amounts of video and robot demonstrations so that robots learn general knowledge far beyond what could be collected on their hardware.

Then an agent practices skills inside that model, trying different actions across imagined scenarios and improving through reinforcement learning. The world model provides physical knowledge, and practice turns that knowledge into skills.

Danijar Hafner and Wilson Yan have spent years developing world models together, and their work includes pioneering research like Dreamer and VideoGPT.

Congrats @danijar, @wilson1yan, and the Embo team!

By @venturetwins, @RaghuRaghuram, and @BornsteinMatt
tweets.quoted_tweet_text:
I'm excited to introduce Embo!

We are building the brain for intelligent robots to help people around the world.

We believe intelligent robots will unlock an era of abundance, making goods and services affordable for everybody. But to deploy them at scale, robots need to work out of the box in unfamiliar scenarios. At Embo, we are building frontier AI models with a deep understanding of physical reality and fine-grained motor skills.

Today's robot skills are fragile. Demonstrations can teach repetitive behaviors, but they cannot cover every object or situation a robot will encounter. We need general pretraining at internet scale to fill the gaps between individual tasks and practice to develop reliable motor skills.

The world models our team has pioneered unlock a path to general robots. Our robot brain pretrains on massive amounts of internet video to learn about objects, physical interactions, and how tasks unfold. It then practices motor skills in diverse imagined scenarios to become robust to unexpected situations.

Our team is behind seminal work in AI including Dreamer, VideoGPT, and Diffusion Forcing, with experience from DeepMind, Meta Superintelligence Labs, NVIDIA Cosmos, Berkeley, and MIT.

We have raised a $110M Seed led by @a16z. We are excited to partner with them, @khoslaventures, DST Global, NVentures (@nvidia), @strikervp,  and other strategic investors to bring reliable intelligent robots out into the world.

@EmboAI

US net equity inflows are up to ~3.0% of GDP, their highest on record in data going back to the 1980s.

Net equity inflows measure foreign purchases of US stocks minus US investors' purchases of foreign equities.

This figure has risen nearly +5.0 percentage points since the 2022 bear market low.

Meanwhile, net debt inflows, which measure foreign purchases of US debt securities, such as Treasuries minus US purchases of foreign debt securities, are down to ~1.8%, their lowest since 2022.

As a result, net equity inflows have surpassed net debt inflows as a % of GDP by the widest margin since the 2008 Financial Crisis.

In other words, foreign investors are increasingly directing money towards US equities rather than US bonds.

Overseas demand for US equities has never been this strong.

To the attendees who traveled from all around the world, it meant a lot to me that you made the trip. Some of my favorite moments were between sessions, when I finally got to meet people in person who have been part of the ITC community for years.

To our speakers, thank you for making the time to join us and for sharing how you think about markets. One of the reasons I wanted to put this conference together was to hear from people who can look at the same market and come to very different conclusions. I appreciated how willing you were to explain your thinking and challenge one another’s views.

A special thank you to Dana Howell @thedanahowell  for organizing the conference. Dana thought through so many of the little details that made people feel welcome. I saw how much care went into bringing the weekend together, and I’m grateful for all of it.

I’m glad we got to spend the weekend together, and I hope to see you again next year.
